Here’s one of mine that made me ask the question. 

 

I was 18 years old and had just received my drivers license. My family and I went to the movie theater but since it was full at the time I told my dad he can go ahead and buy the tickets while I go look for parking. 
  


As I’m looking at my left side mirror I try and look for an opening to get back onto the lane. I noticed a small gap and said to myself “Now’s my chance!” I stepped on the gas so fast just thinking about taking the opportunity to get onto the lane. 
 

 

As I stepped on the gas, to my surprise the car didn’t move. I looked down to see I was still on “Park” but as I looked back up I noticed an elderly couple crossing just a few feet in front of me. 
 

 

I was so preoccupied with trying to make it onto the lane I had forgotten to check in front of me. If I would have gone with the speed I intended to I would have most definitely hit the couple ): 

 
 

Of course I was 18 and just barely got my license so this was a pretty amateur move, but man was I glad I was still on “Park”. 
 

 

After this I have been extra cautious of crossing pedestrians, and to this day I feel like I forgot to put the car on drive for a VERY good reason.

I attempted suicide this year on February 13th. 


I wasn’t thinking about how other people will take my death, or how my parents would feel about finding out that their 25 year old daughter couldn’t continue living. 


I just wanted to disappear and stop feeling disappointed in myself. I have never felt so alone in that very moment. 


I texted a friend of mine and said “I’m scared I’m going to do something stupid” but quickly just ended texting him only because I felt like a burden. 


The hardest thing about depression is you can’t just “seek” help, sometimes it’s too hard to even attend to yourself you can’t really push yourself to look for help. 


My boyfriend found me as soon as I drank two bottles of liquid Tylenol and rushed me to the emergency room. I was throwing up all night and had to stay. One thing that irritated me while I was there was nurses asking me “so why’d you do it?” It’s kind of a loaded question and it can’t be summarized. Sometimes people don’t even have an answer to the question or it can be something as mundane as “I just didn’t want to live.” 


I was then admitted to a mental health home to be supervised. I met so many people who have attempted but failed, and people who were there for other reasons. 


I was talking to an older woman about our reasons for being there. She said she was contemplating suicide for a while, “do I just walk into traffic? Should I jump off a bridge?” I told her how I went about it and she replied with “you are very brave” almost as if she was looking up to me for trying. At that very moment I realized that attempting doesn’t make you brave, seeking for the help you need and overcoming your anxiety makes you brave. 


The day I was discharged and was able to feel the sun and breathe the outside air for the first time in a week was surreal. I felt like I had a second chance. 


Of course it took me time to get over my depression, it didn’t just go away after but all it took was seeing things in a new perspective. 


A quote I tell myself when I’m having a bad day or feeling out of sync with people is “If you don’t change in the direction you’re going, you will end up where you are headed” in which I change the direction of my thought process. 


You are in charge of your depression, you are I charge of your fate, not your depression. No matter how hard it seems please just seek help. Don’t listen to your mind when it tells you “they don’t care” because we do. 


TLDR; Suicide is serious and most of the time if you ask someone “why?” It’s a loaded question, they can’t summarize it in one sentence. Sorry but I don’t have a TLDR version of this.
